clinical.title: Clinical case
clinical.purpose: Review of the whole case: complaints, history, examination, data already available
clinical.binaryNote: Documents and audio recordings are kept in the case, but their content does not reach the analysis: text extraction from PDF and speech transcription are not connected yet. Transfer the key points as text.
checklist: Complaints and how they changed over time
History of the present illness: how it started, what changed
Past medical history, comorbidities, operations
Medications, allergies, intolerances
Examination findings and vital signs
Investigations already performed and their results
What part of the basic work-up is missing
redFlags: Signs of a condition life-threatening within hours
Symptoms requiring malignancy to be ruled out
Drug interactions and contraindications in the prescriptions
Mismatch between severity of complaints and extent of the work-up

labs.title: Laboratory tests
labs.purpose: Interpretation of panels: what deviates significantly, what is secondary, what to recheck
labs.binaryNote: A photo or PDF of the form is kept in the case but does not reach the analysis: form recognition is not connected yet. Enter the values as a panel or paste the result as text.
checklist: Checking every value against the laboratory reference interval
Significance of the deviation: clinically important or borderline
Consistency of the values with one another
Trend compared with previous tests, if available
Effect of medication and sampling conditions on the result
What should be rechecked or added
redFlags: Critical values requiring immediate action
Signs of acute renal or hepatic failure
Sharp fall in haemoglobin, platelets or neutrophils
Electrolyte disturbances dangerous to the heart

xray.title: Radiography
xray.purpose: Review of a radiographic study: description, report, what to clarify
xray.binaryNote: The image is read by a model: it describes what it sees and what is worth checking. This is a second opinion, not a radiologist's report; the absence of visible changes does not mean the absence of pathology.
checklist: Quality and positioning: is the image suitable for conclusions
Completeness of the description by region, not only of the finding
Whether the report follows from the description
Correlation with the clinical picture
Whether additional projections or another study are needed
Comparison with previous images
redFlags: Signs of pneumothorax, free gas, acute pathology
A description containing a finding that is absent from the report
A report not supported by anything in the description

ct.title: Computed tomography
ct.purpose: CT review: completeness of the protocol, whether the report follows the description, what to investigate further
ct.binaryNote: ONE submitted image is read — one reconstruction in one window, already without density data (HU). This is a fragment, not a study: the model cannot scroll the series, measure density or build reconstructions.
checklist: Protocol: contrast phases, scanned region, slice thickness
Completeness of the description for all organs in the region, not only the target
Sizes and locations of findings stated and reproducible
Whether the report follows from the description
Comparison with previous studies and the trend
Indications for contrast and account of renal function
redFlags: Signs of bleeding, ischaemia, perforation, thromboembolism
A mass lesion with no further plan
A finding requiring urgent contact with the treating physician

mri.title: Magnetic resonance imaging
mri.purpose: MRI review: sequences, correlation with the clinical picture, what to clarify
mri.binaryNote: ONE submitted image is read. The model does not see the series of sequences (T1/T2/DWI/FLAIR) or the comparison between them — it looks at a single frame.
checklist: Sequences and modes: are they sufficient for the question
Use of contrast and its justification
Completeness of the description of the region of interest and adjacent structures
Whether the report follows from the description
Correlation with the clinical and neurological status
Trend relative to previous studies
redFlags: Signs of acute cerebrovascular accident
Compression of the spinal cord or cauda equina
A space-occupying process with mass effect

us.title: Ultrasound
us.purpose: Ultrasound review: completeness of the protocol, measurements, what needs clarification
us.binaryNote: A single submitted frame is read. The model does not see loops or motion — frame-by-frame review of a video recording requires a separate model and validation.
checklist: Completeness of the protocol by organs and structures
Presence of measurements and their comparability with the norm
Assessment of blood flow where it is needed
Limitations of the study: acoustic windows, patient preparation
Whether the report follows from the description
Comparison with previous studies
redFlags: Free fluid in the abdominal or pericardial cavity
Signs of deep vein thrombosis
Acute pathology requiring surgical assessment

ecg.title: Electrocardiography
ecg.purpose: ECG review from the description and parameters: rhythm, conduction, ischaemia
ecg.binaryNote: The tracing is read by the model as an image: rhythm, axes and intervals are judged by eye, from the picture. This is not signal analysis: milliseconds and amplitudes are measured by the device, not by a photograph.
checklist: Rhythm, rate, regularity
Electrical axis and rotations
PQ, QRS and corrected QT intervals
Signs of ischaemia, injury, scar
Signs of chamber overload
Comparison with the previous tracing and with the complaints
redFlags: ST elevation and other signs of acute infarction
Life-threatening arrhythmias
QT prolongation dangerous for drug therapy
Complete block with bradycardia

endoscopy.title: Endoscopy
endoscopy.purpose: Review of an endoscopy report: completeness of the examination, biopsies, follow-up
endoscopy.binaryNote: A single submitted frame is read. Frame-by-frame review of a video recording is not connected — the model sees a still, not the procedure.
checklist: Completeness of the examination: how far it reached, what was inspected
Quality of preparation and visibility
Description of findings with location and size
Whether biopsies were taken where indicated
Follow-up plan and timing of the repeat study
Whether the report follows from the description
redFlags: Signs of active bleeding
Suspicion of malignancy without biopsy
Complications of the procedure

histology.title: Histology and cytology
histology.purpose: Review of a pathology report: completeness, staging, what to clarify
histology.binaryNote: The submitted microphotograph is read: what is visible in the frame at this magnification. This is not a pathology report — the diagnosis is made by the pathologist from the whole specimen.
checklist: Type of specimen and its adequacy for a conclusion
Histological type and grade of differentiation
Resection margins and their status
Vascular invasion, perineural invasion, lymph nodes
Immunohistochemistry and molecular markers: were the required ones done
Completeness of the data for staging
redFlags: A malignant process with no statement of resection margins
Specimen declared non-informative with no plan for review
Discrepancy with the clinical and imaging diagnosis

derm.title: Dermatology
derm.purpose: Review of the description of a skin lesion and dermatoscopy: what is concerning
derm.binaryNote: Image assessment by a model is deliberately not connected: the cost of an error in melanoma is too high for an unvalidated model.
checklist: Location, size, shape and borders of the lesion
Colour and its heterogeneity
Change over time
Dermatoscopic features, if dermatoscopy was performed
Associated risk factors and family history
Indications for biopsy or referral to an oncologist
redFlags: ABCDE features concerning for melanoma
Rapid growth, bleeding, ulceration
Change in a long-standing lesion
